imageDigestUpdateTitle: The "{tag}" tag now points to a newer image than the one pulled
imageUpdateCheckSetting: Check registries for image updates periodically
imageUpdateCheckHelp: Looks for a newer image behind each service's current tag and, if enabled, for newer tags of the same form (e.g. 1.2.3-alpine → 1.2.4-alpine). Per service, use the labels dockge.update.enable=false, dockge.update.watch_tags=true|false, dockge.update.include_tags and dockge.update.exclude_tags (regexes, separated by ;). diun.* labels (including diun.watch_repo) work too.
imageNewTagsHint: Change the tag in the compose file to move up
updatesBoardHint: Stacks with a newer image or newer tags
primaryHostnameHelp: Used to build links to published ports
disableAuthHelp: Only for setups where another layer, like a reverse proxy, handles sign-in
globalEnvHelp: Variables here are available to every stack, alongside each stack's own .env
Frontend Version do not match backend ve: Frontend and backend versions differ, reload the page after updating
imageUpdateCardHelp: Dockge asks each image's registry whether a newer image or newer tags exist. Nothing is pulled until you update a stack.
imageUpdateWatchTagsLabel: List newer tags for every service
checkAllHelp: Runs a check for every stack on this server
perServiceLabelsHelp: Add these to a service in its compose file. The diun.* equivalents work too.
labelWatchTagsHelp: List newer tags for this service
labelIncludeHelp: Only consider tags matching these regexes, separated by ;
updateNoticeHelp: Shows a notice in the header when a new release is out
releasesHelp: Every release with its list of changes
settingsRegistriesDescription: Sign in to private image registries
registriesHelp: Dockge uses these logins for pulls, deploys and image update checks on this server.
registriesNoneHelp: Public images work without signing in
registrySignInHelp: Runs docker login for Dockge, which checks the credentials with the registry.
registryPasswordHelp: An access token is safer, e.g. a GitHub token with read:packages
settingsLinkedDescription: Other Dockge servers you can move stacks to
linkedServersHelp: Stacks can be moved to these servers. Their stacks stay separate and never show up in your list here.
linkedServersNoneHelp: Link another Dockge below to move stacks to it
linkCannotReceive: Connected, but that Dockge can't receive stacks, update it to this version
linkRemoveConfirm: Unlink {name}? Stacks already moved there are not affected.
linkAddHelp: Signs in to the other Dockge once and keeps only a sign-in token, never the password.
linkAddressHelp: Where this server reaches the other Dockge
linkNameHelp: Shown when you pick where to move a stack
linkUsernameHelp: An account on the other Dockge
linkPasswordHelp: Used once to sign in, not stored
moveIntro: Stops the stack, copies its folder and named volumes with owners and permissions intact, and starts it on the other server. The stopped copy stays here until you remove it.
moveChecksPassed: {name} is ready to receive this stack
moveHereStays: Stopped copy, kept until you remove it
moveKeepOpen: The move continues if you close this tab
moveDoneHelp: The stopped copy is still here. Remove it once you've checked the stack on the other server.
moveFailedHelp: Nothing was left behind on the other server, and the stack runs here again if it ran before.
movedBannerHint: {when}. This copy is stopped and kept as a fallback.
movedRemoveConfirm: Remove the stopped copy of this stack from this server? Its folder and the named volumes that were moved to {name} are deleted here. This can't be undone.
cleanupIntro: What docker system prune --all would remove on this server, group by group. Nothing is removed until you confirm.
cleanupLoading: Looking at containers, images and networks…
cleanupContainersHelp: Containers of stopped stacks. Starting a stack again recreates them.
cleanupImagesHelp: Untagged image layers left behind by pulls and builds. Always safe to remove.
cleanupImagesAllHelp: Every image no running container uses. Stacks pull what they need again when they start.
cleanupStoppedOnlyHelp: Only used by stopped containers that are removed too
cleanupNetworksHelp: Networks no running container is connected to. Compose creates them again on start.
cleanupVolumesHelp: Volumes without a name that no container uses. Their data is deleted for good. Named volumes are never touched.
cleanupVolumesUnsupported: Needs Docker 23 or newer, this server runs {version}
cleanupConfirmStacks: These stopped stacks lose their containers and start fresh next time: {stacks}
